correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the minimum and maximum reduces the symmetric sample-variance calculation to fixed endpoints 0 and 1 plus n-2 iid uniform interior points. Their first two power moments give the exact coefficient. The beta law of the normalized range then gives all needed moments. The standard exact variance identity for unbiased sample variance with uniform second and fourth central moments produces the comparison formula. Exact rational replay for every integer 2<=n<=250 checks all displayed finite-n identities; the infinite quantifier rests on the algebraic proof, not on enumeration.

value.rationale: Range and sample variance are canonical competing spread summaries, and reconstructing variance from range information is a long-standing practical problem. The exact uniform identity identifies the best L2 predictor of the realized sample variance from the range alone, produces an unbiased population-variance estimator automatically, and quantifies a nonregular efficiency gain of order n relative to ordinary sample variance. The result is structural rather than a table recomputation: it explains why endpoint information becomes disproportionately informative about scale in a bounded uniform family.
